the design of healthcare support systems for caregivers should consider the following aspects: 1) a user-friendly and easy-to-use interface; 2) a clear and effective communication system for caregivers and ALF inhabitants; 3) a system for managing notes and reminders for daily activities; 4) a monitoring system for ALF inhabitants; and 5) a system that allows caregivers to manage and control the use of the system.

The main takeaway from our work is that

, in addition to the technical and social challenges, designing systems for caregivers requires an in-depth knowledge of the caregivers’ daily activities and their needs, as well as a thorough understanding of the ALFs’ organizational structure.

, to be effective in supporting caregivers, systems must be able to provide them with a comprehensive view of the daily activities of ALF inhabitants and of the assistance tasks that caregivers have already performed, while also providing caregivers with a means to communicate and collaborate with each other.
